## Session note v3226
- Continued the top-down refinement pass with the next quotation after the Pauline triad: **Aquinas — "To love is to will the good of the other."**
- Kept the live wording unchanged this pass.
- Reconfirmed the archive's earlier lexical decision that `cuxna` is better than `djica` here for **will**, because the line is about chosen willing rather than mere wanting; and re-confirmed that `xamgu be de` still carries **the good of the other / what is good for the other** more cleanly than a more compressed alternative.

Locked live wording:

```lojban id="v3226-refinement-aquinas-will-the-good-of-the-other"
.i lo nu da prami de cu du lo nu da cuxna lo xamgu be de
```

Best compact reading:

**To love is to will the good of the other.**

Why the wording currently stands:

- The standard dictionary tradition still glosses `prami` as **x1 loves/feels strong affectionate devotion towards x2**, so keeping `da ... de` explicit still matters here: the sentence is not about an impersonal occurrence of love, but about one lover in relation to one beloved.
- The same dictionary tradition glosses `cuxna` as **x1 chooses/selects x2 from a set/sequence of alternatives x3**, which is why it still fits **will** better than `djica`; the English point is not simply wanting the good, but actively willing/choosing it.
- `xamgu` is still glossed as **x1 is good/beneficial for x2 by standard x3**, so `lo xamgu be de` continues to say **what is good for the other person**, which is the right pressure for Aquinas's line.
- Keeping the sentence as a definitional identity with `du` still feels right here: the quotation is not merely offering a frequent association of love with beneficence, but a compressed account of what loving *is*.

So the best active reading still remains: **loving someone is choosing / willing what is good for that other person.**

- The standard dictionary tradition also glosses `gleki` as **x1 is happy/merry/glad/gleeful about x2 (event/state)** and `pluka` as **x1 pleases x2 under conditions x3**, which is why `lo nu de gleki ... cu pluka da` still keeps the relation oriented correctly: the other's happiness is what pleases the lover.

- Keeping the sentence as a definitional identity with `du` still feels right here as well: Leibniz's line is offering a compressed account of what loving *is*.

```lojban id="v3275-refinement-footnote-eu"
<<footnotes "eu" ".i na zasti lo nu lo prenu cu mulno fi lo ka zoi gy. eudaimonia .gy gi'e na se krinu. .i ku'i sei badri lo du'u ti cu simlu lo nu na mapti .i su'o palci prenu cu kakne lo nu snada lo ka zoi gy. eudaimonia .gy zmadu su'o vrude prenu (mi ji'a na fanta lo nu mi jinvi lo du'u lo palci prenu cu so'i roi zmadu lo vrude prenu le ka gleki). .i ji'a cumki lo nu lo remna poi na prenu cu snada lo ka zoi gy. eudaimonia .gy gi'e na pensi fi lo krinu ki'u lo nu no lo krinu poi se srana lo se bilga cu zasti fo lo remna poi na prenu noi na du lo si'o xamgu .e lo si'o drani. .i lo se ciksi be lo se zasti cu banzu.">>
```

Best compact reading:

**There is no unjustified complete eudaimonia as a person. Unfortunately, however unfair it may be, some evil agents can achieve higher degrees of eudaimonia than some morally virtuous agents (I'm even open to the possibility that evil persons are generally happier). It is also possible to flourish as a non-person human without considering justification because there is no prescriptive justification (only descriptive explanation) for non-persons (with the only exceptions being The Good and The Right).**

Why the wording now stands this way:

- `mulno` keeps **complete** explicit.
- `palci` keeps **evil** on the moral-standard axis rather than merely the bad/unpleasant axis.
- `vrude` keeps **virtuous** explicitly moral.
- `prenu` versus `remna` preserves the crucial archive distinction between **person** and **human**.
- `krinu` and the closing `lo se ciksi be lo se zasti cu banzu` preserve the contrast between prescriptive justification and merely descriptive explanation.
- `zmadu` and `gleki` keep the comparative and happiness clauses explicit without forcing a more ornate paraphrase.

So the best active reading now is: **complete flourishing without justification is unavailable *as a person*; nevertheless some evil persons may flourish more, and even be happier, than some virtuous persons; and non-person humans may still flourish descriptively, because prescriptive justification does not apply to them in the same way.**

```lojban id="v3309-refinement-neurochemical-reward-intentionality-sacrifice"
  tezu'e lo nu se cpacu lo se pluka be lo xadni

  .i ri du lo menli tcini poi platu lo nu zukte
```

Best compact reading:

**Love is more than a risk toward a neurochemical reward for cooperative behavior: it is intentionality which sacrificially overrides all other reasons, including our own happiness.**

Why the wording still stands:

- `lo nu ckape` still keeps **risk** on the event/state axis rather than forcing a brittle thing-like noun.

- `lo menli tcini poi platu lo nu zukte` still remains the archive's most disciplined way to paraphrase **intentionality** without pretending there is one perfectly canonical single-word equivalent.
- `bapli lo nu ro lo drata mukti cu na se pilno tezu'e lo nu zukte` still preserves the later stronger archive reading of **override** as compelling competing reasons not to be used in guiding action.
- `ta'i lo nu dunda lo se banzu be lo sevzi lo drata` still keeps the sacrificial axis explicit by making self-giving the mode of that override.
- `lo nu mi'a gleki cu cmima le'i drata mukti poi na se pilno tezu'e lo nu zukte` still keeps **including our own happiness** literal and visible instead of letting it disappear into abstraction.
- So the best active reading still remains: **love is not reducible to a risky reach toward a pleasant bodily payoff from cooperation; rather, it is a deliberate action-guiding intentionality that can, through self-giving, force competing motives aside even when one of those motives is our own happiness.**

- `sinma` still best preserves the **respect / esteem** axis.

- `pagbu` still best preserves **part / component**.
- `stodi` plus `smadi ma ba fasnu` still keep the note on the **some predictability of stable identity** axis rather than collapsing it into generic reliability.
- `jinvi ... banli pe'a` still remains the archive's best conservative handle for **idealize**, because it keeps the move explicitly on the side of judgment or taking-as-great rather than falsely claiming an official one-word equivalent.
- `jimpe lo du'u ma smuni lo nu prami` still keeps the final clause centered on **understanding what it means to love**.

So the best active reading still remains: **love is not just trust, nor merely respect for what someone has made or chosen of themselves; respect and some stable identity-predictability belong to love, and we often need a certain idealization in order to understand what loving that person means.**
